findings.title: website_name leaks the website domain and path for TL0 users that anonymous viewers should not see
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), so for a TL0 user seen by an anonymous viewer the raw website URL is omitted on purpose. The new `website_name` attribute is added to the public attribute list (line 43) but not to that untrusted list. `include_website_name` (lines 153-155) only checks `website.present?`, so for the same user the serializer now emits `website_name`, which contains the host and, with this PR, the full URL path (e.g. `example.com/user`). The untrusted-attributes spec (spec line 11) also omits `website_name`, and the TL0 fixture sets no website, so the existing test cannot catch this. Result: the anti-spam hiding of new users' websites for anonymous visitors is bypassed, and the domain and path are exposed in public user JSON and the profile header.

findings.title: Same-parent-domain check matches unrelated sites that share a multi-label public suffix
findings.body: The branch at lines 144-146 treats two hosts as the same site when they have the same label count and everything after the first label matches. Take an instance at `mysite.github.io` and a profile website `other.github.io/about`. Both hosts have 3 labels and `github.io == github.io`, so the full path is shown for an unrelated site (`other.github.io/about` instead of `other.github.io`). The same happens for `mysite.co.uk` vs `other.co.uk`. The intent was www./forum. siblings under one registrable domain, but the check does not account for public suffixes, so it shows paths for other sites on shared hosting domains.

findings.title: Hostname comparison is case-sensitive, so the same-domain path rule can miss
findings.body: `URI#host` returns the host as written and does not lowercase it. A website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an instance whose hostname is `example.com` fails `website_host == discourse_host` at line 141. It then falls through to the else branch, which returns plain `Example.com` with no path, even though the domain matches. Both sides should be normalized (e.g. with `downcase`) before comparing.

findings.title: website_name is not refreshed after the user saves a new website, so the header can show the old domain
findings.body: The template now renders `model.website_name` (user.hbs line 66), which is computed only on the server. Previously the controller derived the name from `model.website`, which updated reactively. `save()` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response (line 210), so after a user changes their website in preferences, `website_name` on the shared model stays stale. The profile header keeps showing the old domain until the user record is refetched, which a sibling-route transition may not do.

findings.title: Branches and edge cases of website_name are untested
findings.body: The new specs only cover one website (`example.com/user`) against three hostnames. Not covered: the equal-label-count branch for `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com` (serializer lines 144-146), a blank website where `website_name` should be nil, an unparseable website, and mixed-case hosts. The untrusted-attribute spec (line 11) also does not include `website_name`, so the TL0 anonymous visibility problem is not checked. Regressions in the branch logic or visibility rules would go unnoticed.
